title: A Sunny Day
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'ay' (the /ai/ sound at the end of a word)
note_for_grown_ups: This is a Phase 5 book. It uses the new sound 'ay' — another way to write the /ai/ sound children already know from 'rain', used at the END of a word (day, play, hay). Every other word only uses sounds taught in Phases 2 to 4, so it is fully decodable at this point.

pages.text: It was a hot, sunny day.
pages.illustration: Wide, bleached-bright summer scene: a farm field under a huge white-hot sky, heat shimmer over the stubble. Almost too bright to look at.

pages.text: Pip and Ned ran to play.
pages.illustration: Pip and Ned running side by side through the field, wings and flippers out, pure joy. Grass seeds flying up around them.
A tall stack of golden hay bales, Ned scrambling up the side with his feet slipping on the loose straw. Big warm gold shapes.

pages.text: Pip sat on the soft hay.
pages.illustration: Pip sunk deep into loose hay at the top of the stack with just his head and tuft showing, blissful. Fine straw detail.

pages.text: Ned had fun in the pool.
pages.illustration: Ned launching into a shallow blue paddling pool with all four limbs out, water leaping up in a crown shape. Peak duckling.
The wave of water arriving at Pip, who is caught mid-flinch with one wing up. Ned in the pool grinning. Comic timing.

pages.text: Pip did not stay in the sun.
pages.illustration: Pip stalking away from the pool with wet, spiky, indignant feathers, tail up. Ned's splashes still going on behind him.

pages.text: Pip ran to a cool spot.
pages.illustration: Pip settled in deep cool shade under a broad leafy bush, seen from outside so the shade is a rich dark green pocket in a blazing page.

pages.text: Fun in the sun all day!
pages.illustration: Closing page: both of them flat on their backs in the shade at end of day, exhausted and happy, the sun going low and orange over the field.
